message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated American composers across different eras:

| Era | Composer | Notable Works |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| **19th‑early 20th century** | **John Philip Sousa** (1854–1932) | “The Stars and Stripes Forever,” “Washington Post March” |
| | **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris” |
| | **Samuel Barber** (1910–1981) | “Adagio for Strings,” “Knoxville: Summer of 1915” |
| **Mid‑20th century** | **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man” |
| | **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | “West Side Story,” “Candide” |
| | **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | “Einstein on the Beach,” “Glassworks” |
| **Late 20th‑21st century** | **John Adams** (born 1947) | “Nixon in China,” “Short Ride in a Fast Machine” |
| | **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | “Music for 18 Musicians,” “Different Trains” |
| | **Jennifer Higdon** (born 1962) | “Blue Cathedral,” “Piano Concerto” |

These figures have shaped American orchestral, operatic, film, and popular music traditions, earning international acclaim and influencing generations of musicians.
